<thought>Based on the mass spectrum, the neutral molecular weight is ~182 Da. The 13C NMR shows nine distinct carbons: one carbonyl (~169 ppm), six aromatic carbons (≈123–133 ppm), and two aliphatic carbons (≈43 and 26 ppm). This pattern fits a C₉H₁₀O₄ formula (9 C, 10 H, 4 O) which gives a molecular weight of 182 Da and a DBE of 5 (aromatic ring 4 + carbonyl 1). The structure that matches these data is **ethyl 4‑hydroxybenzoate** (also known as ethyl p‑hydroxybenzoate). Its SMILES string is `CCOC(=O)C1=CC=C(C=C1)O`. This provides the observed carbonyl, aromatic, and ethoxy aliphatic signals.</thought>
<final_answer>CCOC(=O)C1=CC=C(C=C1)O</final_answer>
